assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new instrument that opened a door: the magic-wavelength optical lattice lets thousands of atoms be interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, taking clocks to ~1e-18 fractional uncertainty. The invention is original, sharply defined and underpins relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a coming redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2001-2003 and first demonstrated it with Sr; Ye's group drove it to the highest accuracy and stability. Both credited names are essential and the two-person configuration is clean. I recall other contributors (e.g. Takamoto, Ludlow, Kimble-related work) but the supplied credit is adequate.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of independent confirmation in many laboratories with Sr, Yb and others; the interpretation is stable and the technique is already operational. Timely, and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a continuation of the 2005 frequency-comb prize (Hall, Hansch) rather than a separate invention.
Ye also appears on other ballot entries; I have not checked how that affects prize combinations.
My recollection of the earliest priority claims is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators are a new class of matter whose existence was predicted and then directly seen. The quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells and the 3D Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 surface states seen by ARPES are concrete experiments showing protected edge and surface conduction. The field changed how materials are classified and has lasting impact on spintronics and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: The credit is awkward. Kane (with Mele) supplied the theory; Molenkamp's group provided the first transport observation in 2007 (following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not in the supplied names); Hasan led the first 3D observation by ARPES. I choose Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, which pairs the theory with the two original experiments, but this leaves out Mele, who shares the original Z2 theory with Kane, and the Zhang group and others for the HgTe proposal and Bi2Se3 work.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups over more than fifteen years; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, though prize-worthiness of the full topological-matter field is still rather broad.
uncertainties: Fair division between the 2D and 3D discoveries and between theory and experiment; the three-name limit forces exclusions.
Priority between the Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 ARPES and transport work is contested in the literature and I cannot settle it from the supplied text.
Overlap with B004 and B045 variants of the same topic means the final configuration may be settled elsewhere.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are a topologically protected spin texture first seen by small-angle neutron scattering in MnSi, then imaged in real space by Lorentz TEM and, in a different system, by spin-polarised STM at atomic scale. These are original observations with direct visual proof, and the work started a large field of topological spintronics and possible low-power memory concepts.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer (with Boni, Muhlbauer) made the first experimental observation of the lattice in a bulk magnet; Tokura's group (Yu et al.) gave real-space TEM images and room-temperature stability; Wiesendanger's group showed atomic-scale skyrmion lattices and writing and deleting single skyrmions. The theory by Bogdanov and colleagues is outside the supplied credit. The three-name configuration is defensible but excludes the original theorists and some experimental co-authors.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by neutron scattering, TEM, STM and Hall-effect signatures in many materials. The technological application (racetrack memory) is not yet realised, so the benefit remains prospective.
uncertainties: Theory priority (Bogdanov) is not captured by the supplied credit.
Practical applications remain unproven.
I have not independently verified the precise dates of the first real-space observations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a theoretical flat-band prediction into a platform with superconductivity and correlated insulators from a tunable angle. It is a new door to strongly correlated physics in a clean, controllable material, and it was a genuine surprise experiment. The discovery is clear and has spawned moire materials broadly.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Yuan Cao as first author) observed correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. The supplied credit pairs theory and experiment and fits a three-person prize. Other contributors (Kim, Dean and Yazdani groups for early confirmation and imaging) may deserve mention, and the early moire work of others is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several groups within a few years; the pairing mechanism for the superconductivity remains unsettled, so the interpretation is not fully stable. Timely but perhaps somewhat early.
uncertainties: The origin of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Whether the committee would credit theory for a prediction that did not itself identify superconductivity.
Reproducibility of device quality across laboratories is variable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single colour-centre spins, especially the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, are optically read out and coherently controlled at room temperature. This gives quantum sensors with nanoscale spatial resolution for magnetic fields, temperature and strain, and spin qubits. For a microscopist this is a powerful new tool that lets people see phenomena at the nanoscale that were previously out of reach.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group made the original optical detection of single NV spins in 1997; Awschalom extended coherent control and the wider colour-centre platform (including SiC); Walsworth drove ensemble NV magnetometry and imaging. Lukin, also credited to this entry, contributed key theory and experiments but appears on other ballots. I would choose the three with the clearest experimental claims, but the allocation among Wrachtrup, Awschalom and the sensing community is not obviously settled.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups confirm and extend the results; the technology is moving into commercial sensors. The field is mature, although the prize-worthy single discovery is diffuse.
uncertainties: The discovery is spread over many people and applications; a single crisp invention is hard to identify.
Different credit for quantum sensing versus qubit control may require a split.
Early priority between the 1997 detection and related Australian and German work is not verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are a clear invention with enormous practical consequences for motors, wind turbines, hard disks and electric vehicles. They are by far the strongest commercially used permanent magnets. This matches the requirement that a prize should benefit humanity and be based on an original, verified invention rather than a refinement.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo) and Croat (General Motors) independently developed Nd2Fe14B in 1983-84 by different routes (sintered versus melt-spun). That near-simultaneous independent discovery makes a shared award natural, and both credited names are the right ones. I recall that Herbst and collaborators also contributed to the structure determination, but they are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of industrial use and confirmation. Recognition is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: It is more a materials engineering invention than a conceptual physics advance, so physics-scope may be contested.
Patent and priority disputes between the two companies are not resolved in what I know.
Supply constraints and sustainability of rare earths are not part of the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic-resolution force microscopy with the qPlus sensor, and especially CO-tip imaging of molecular structure, made it possible to see chemical bonds and the geometry of individual molecules. This is a measurement tool that opened a door in a way that is very familiar to a microscopist, and the images are directly interpretable.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor and demonstrated sub-angstrom-oscillation operation; Gross and Meyer, at IBM Zurich, showed the chemical structure of a single molecule in 2009 and subsequent bond-order imaging. The credit is reasonable for a three-person prize. Others, such as Pavlicek, and Gross's collaborators, may argue for inclusion and are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced in many laboratories; the interpretation of contrast (Pauli repulsion, electrostatics) is well understood. Mature, with ongoing applications to on-surface chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a tool improvement over the 1986 AFM and STM prizes rather than a new discovery.
Whether the Nobel scope is better suited to chemistry.
Priority of qPlus versus other tuning-fork-based sensors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical high-energy neutrinos and of the blazar TXS 0506+056 opened neutrino astronomy at energies far above what the 2002 and 2015 prizes covered. The measurement is a real experimental discovery based on a very large instrument built in Antarctic ice, and it adds an entirely new channel for observing the universe.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the conception and construction of IceCube by Halzen, who proposed and led it, and Karle, who was central in its detector and analysis; in practice it is a collaboration-scale discovery of hundreds of people, which the committee must handle carefully. The two supplied names are the plausible leaders, but others (e.g. the AMANDA pioneers, the observation and analysis leads) could argue.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse astrophysical flux is confirmed in several analyses; the source identification is still limited to a few objects (TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068, plus galactic plane evidence), so source science is still maturing.
uncertainties: Which individuals are to be credited for a large collaboration result.
Only a few sources have been identified, so the astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.
Independent confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal is still limited.
